record.paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: outlier handling for single-LEO RTT location verification
record.original_question: How should single-LEO round-trip-time positioning for non-terrestrial-network (NTN) location verification handle user equipment located near the satellite orbit where geometric dilution of precision is poor, so that median performance can satisfy the 10 km verification target without leaving severe outlier users with much worse position error?

evidence.quote: This result illustrates that a single satellite RTT is enough to satisfy the requirement of 10km positioning accuracy for network location verification.

The significant difference between the mean and median PEB values indicates that for certain users, located near the satellite orbit and observe worse GDOP, the positioning accuracy is far worse than the central tendency.
Although it is not clear how to handle such users if single LEO positioning is used in step 6 (Fig. 2(b)), this makes a strong case for multi-LEO positioning, which we discuss next.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite moving along a known orbit, used to verify the position of a ground user equipment (UE) via round-trip-time (RTT) measurements. Model the UE as a point on or near the Earth's surface with unknown horizontal position p ∈ R^2 (altitude assumed known), and let the satellite at the i-th measurement epoch be at known position s_i ∈ R^3, i = 1,…,N. The measurement model is

   r_i = ||s_i − [p; h]|| + c·b + n_i,

where b is an unknown clock-bias term, c the speed of light, and n_i ~ N(0, σ^2) independent Gaussian noise. The position error bound (PEB) is defined as PEB(p) = sqrt(tr(J(p)^{-1})), where J(p) is the Fisher information matrix of the RTT measurement model with respect to p (after marginalising or jointly estimating b). For UEs whose horizontal location lies near the projection of the satellite's orbital ground track, the geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) degenerates and PEB(p) becomes very large, so that although the median PEB over a uniform UE distribution satisfies a 10 km verification accuracy target, the mean PEB and worst-case PEB are an order of magnitude larger.

Design a single-LEO RTT-based positioning and verification procedure—comprising the choice of measurement epochs {t_i}, an estimator p̂ of p, and a verification test deciding whether a claimed location is consistent with the RTT measurements—that meets the following requirements simultaneously:

(i) the median horizontal positioning error over a uniform distribution of UEs on the visible portion of Earth is at most 10 km;

(ii) the fraction of UEs (including those located near the sub-satellite orbital track where GDOP is poor) whose horizontal positioning error exceeds 10 km is bounded by a prescribed small ε > 0;

(iii) the procedure uses only one LEO satellite (no multi-satellite fusion).

Alternatively, prove that no such procedure exists, i.e., establish a fundamental lower bound showing that for any single-LEO RTT estimator the worst-case PEB on a positive-measure set of UE locations must exceed 10 km whenever the median PEB meets the 10 km target.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research question concerning how to mitigate severe outliers in single-LEO RTT-based location verification when geometric dilution of precision is poor. No publication was identified that resolves the question for the strict single-LEO setting; subsequent work on NTN/LEO localization typically proposes multi-LEO or hybrid solutions rather than guaranteeing the worst-case 10 km target with a single satellite.
